justice: The corridor allocates substantial space to motor traffic with multiple wide vehicle lanes, while pedestrian space is only visible at the edges behind hedges and a fence, suggesting an imbalanced distribution of street space for all users.

A bus stop shelter is visible on the left side, which supports more equitable access to public transport for non-drivers, but no corresponding crossing facility is visible from this viewpoint to connect both sides of the road fairly.

The right side shows a separated side path behind a hedge and decorative fence, indicating some protected space for non-motor users, yet the fence and planted strips may also limit direct access points and route flexibility.
No curb ramps, tactile paving, marked crosswalks, or other barrier-free crossing details are visible in the image, so accessibility for a broad range of users cannot be rated highly.
Lane markings for vehicles are clear and continuous, while pedestrian priority elements are not visible, indicating rules and design are more legible for drivers than for people moving on foot.

A bus stop is visible on the left, but no marked pedestrian crossing or refuge island is visible nearby, which can create risk where transit users need to cross a broad carriageway.
livability: Dense rows of mature trees on both sides create a green boulevard character that improves everyday environmental quality and makes the corridor more pleasant.
